draft.title: Controlling the spread of disease
card: To control a disease, scientists first identify the pathogen that causes it. They then find its host, the organism it lives in, and how it passes from one host to another.
Knowing how it spreads shows where to break the chain. Some pathogens spread by direct contact, by droplets in the air, in contaminated water or food, or by a vector such as a mosquito.
keeping people or animals that may be infected apart from others, so they cannot pass the pathogen on.
actions such as handwashing, clean water and safe food handling, which stop a pathogen reaching a new host. Treatment, such as antibiotics for bacteria, cures infected hosts and so reduces spread.
draft.remember: Find the pathogen, host and route of spread, then block the route.

a.q: Why does a health team work out how a pathogen spreads before choosing a control measure?
opts: So the measure can block the route the pathogen takes
So the pathogen can be grown in the laboratory
So every host can be given the same treatment
So the pathogen's host can be named correctly
a.why: A control measure works by breaking the chain between hosts, so the team must know where that chain can be broken. Naming the host matters too, but it does not show which measure will stop transmission.
a.clue: Think about what each measure is trying to interrupt.

b.q: An outbreak of a stomach illness in a town in Gippsland is traced to a pathogen in a shared water supply. Which action targets how it spreads?
opts: Supplying treated drinking water to households
Giving antibiotics to everyone living in the town
Keeping only the ill people from school and work
Testing food in every café for the pathogen
b.why: The pathogen spreads through contaminated water, so clean water stops it reaching new hosts. Keeping ill people away from others is quarantine, which may help a little, but it does not deal with the water source that is infecting people.
b.clue: Which action deals with the route the pathogen takes?

a.best: So the measure can block the route the pathogen takes

b.best: Supplying treated drinking water to households

problems.detail: Why (b) calls keeping ill people away from others 'quarantine'. Separating people known to be ill is isolation. Quarantine, as the card itself defines it, is for people who may be infected. This blurs the card's definition.
The option 'Keeping only the ill people from school and work' is awkwardly worded. 'Only' could be read as 'just the ill people' or as 'doing only this', which may confuse students.

check.summary: Both questions have one clearly correct answer. Why (b) labels keeping ill people away as quarantine when that is isolation, and the 'Keeping only the ill people' option is awkwardly worded.
